items.summary: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. In the Department's view, the best reading of ERISA's exclusive purpose provision is and has always been that a plan fiduciary may not start with an ulterior motive or consider any factors collateral to plan participants' financial interests during any part of the process of making investment-selection decisions. The proposal would strengthen the fiduciary standards of pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA as instructed in President Trump's Executive Order 14366, Protecting American Investors from Foreign-Owned and Politically Motivated Proxy Advisors.

items.summary: Although the consolidated audit trail (the "CAT") continues to be a necessary regulatory tool, its decentralized governance has presented certain challenges to administering the CAT. To address those shortcomings, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") proposes to assume direct control of the CAT. Specifically, the Commission is proposing amendments to Regulation NMS under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ("Exchange Act") that would rescind Rule 613, which obligates the national securities exchanges and national securities associations (collectively, the "SROs") to act jointly to develop a national market system plan to develop, implement, and maintain the CAT (the "CAT NMS Plan"). The Commission is simultaneously proposing new Rule 17a-26, which would require the SROs and broker-dealers to record and electronically report to a central repository substantially the same information that was previously required to be recorded and reported pursuant to Rule 613, the CAT NMS Plan, related SRO compliance rules, and related exemptive relief previously issued by the Commission.
items.title: Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail

items.summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) is revising its regulations addressing the circumstances under which a request for rehearing is denied absent Commission action within a particular time frame. Currently, the Commission's regulations provide that unless the Commission acts upon a request for rehearing within 30 days after the request is filed, the request is denied. As revised in this final rule, the regulation will apply only to matters subject to the rehearing and judicial review provisions in the Federal Power Act (FPA) and Natural Gas Act (NGA).

items.summary: This document announces and initiates an EPA effort to streamline the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) permit program and to remove associated barriers to redevelopment. This effort will satisfy an Agency Priority Goal established by the EPA Administrator to streamline the permitting process and improve efficiencies to unleash economic growth. In this document, EPA seeks information to help identify inefficiencies in the permit process and ideas for streamlining, including ideas that would reduce the time, uncertainty, and costs involved in issuing a permit. EPA also seeks information to help identify situations where the RCRA permit presents barriers to redevelopment of and/or parceling of RCRA treatment, storage, and disposal facilities, and ideas to overcome those barriers. EPA will consider information submitted as it develops a plan to address the inefficiencies in, and barriers presented by, the current RCRA permit program. This document also announces four virtual public engagement sessions that will supplement the request for information by providing individual participants an opportunity to provide oral comments on these issues as well.

items.summary: In this document, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau (Bureau) invites interested parties to comment on whether the proposed Relocation Coordinator selected by the eligible space station operators in the Upper C-band satisfies the criteria established by the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) in Upper C-band (3.98-4.2 GHz); Expanding Flexible Use of the 3.7 to 4.2 GHz Band, GN Docket Nos. 25-59 and 18-122, Report and Order, Order of Proposed Modification, and Order on Reconsideration, FCC 26-46 (July 24, 2026) (Upper C-band R&O). In the Upper C-band R&O, the Commission adopted rules to make 160 megahertz of mid-band spectrum available for flexible use throughout the contiguous United States by transitioning incumbent Fixed Satellite Service (FSS) operations out of 4.0-4.16 GHz. The Upper C-band R&O required eligible space station operators to select a Relocation Coordinator that will be responsible for managing the overall transition and coordinating relocation actions among eligible FSS space station operators, incumbent FSS earth station operators, and new Upper C-band flexible use licensees.
items.title: Wireless Telecommunications Bureau Seeks Comment on Whether Proposed Upper C-Band Relocation Coordinator Satisfies Selection Criteria
